author: maya
text: Kicking off Sprint 1. Top item for me is ticket export (BD-101): admins should be able to download the last 30 days of tickets as CSV. Customers keep asking for it.

author: sofia
text: I can take the backend for BD-101. Columns id, subject, status, created_at to start?

author: maya
text: Yes, that's what's in the ticket. Kenji, can you do the button in the list view (BD-102)?

author: kenji
text: Sure, I'll pick up the export button once Sofia's endpoint shape is settled.

author: liam
text: Acme Corp asked whether the export will include who each ticket is assigned to. Without that they can't do per-agent reporting.

author: maya
text: Good call. Let's add an assignee column to the export. I'm updating BD-101 now.

author: maya
text: Done, BD-101 now lists assignee as a required column.

author: sofia
text: Export endpoint skeleton is up locally. Streaming the CSV so big accounts don't time out.

author: liam
text: Just came off calls with Acme and Globex about the export. Both said 30 days is useless for quarterly business reviews, and they need their custom fields in the file too, not just the standard columns.

author: arjun
text: How far back do they need? Unbounded ranges would be expensive.

author: liam
text: A year would cover every case I've heard.

author: maya
text: Decision: the export must support any custom date range up to 12 months (not a fixed 30 days), and it must include all custom fields as extra columns. Arjun, can you make sure the team knows?

author: arjun
text: 👍 will raise it at standup tomorrow.

author: kenji
text: While we're on export, should we also offer XLSX? Some users open CSVs in Excel and complain about encoding.

author: maya
text: Not this quarter. CSV with UTF-8 BOM should fix the Excel encoding issue. Let's park XLSX.

author: sofia
text: PR for the export endpoint is up: last 30 days, CSV, id/subject/status/created_at/assignee. Reviews welcome.

author: arjun
text: LGTM, merging. Nice work on the streaming.

author: kenji
text: Export button is wired into the ticket list now, calls Sofia's endpoint. Opening a PR.

author: liam
text: Acme tried the new export and it only gives them 30 days, and no custom fields. I thought we agreed on 12 months?

author: maya
text: Second big item for Sprint 1 is SLA alerts, BD-103: when a ticket breaches its SLA we email the assignee. BD-104 covers the settings page where admins set SLA hours per priority.

author: dev
text: I'll take BD-103. Probably a periodic job that checks open tickets against their deadlines.

author: dev
text: Talked to a couple of support leads at Acme. They said an email *at* breach is too late; by then the customer is already annoyed. They want a heads-up before it happens, somewhere the team actually looks.

author: zara
text: Also email notifications get filtered into folders nobody reads, from what I've seen in testing.

author: maya
text: Agreed. Let's change it: send the warning 15 minutes BEFORE the breach, and post it to the team's Slack channel instead of email. We drop email notifications for this entirely.

author: arjun
text: ok, agreed. Dev, that changes your job a bit.

author: dev
text: Makes sense, noted.

author: dev
text: SLA notifier PR is up, using the existing mailer so it was quick.

author: kenji
text: SLA settings page (BD-104) is done: per-priority hours, validation, saves to the org settings.

author: zara
text: Testing SLA alerts: the notification fires at breach and it's an email. Wasn't it supposed to warn before breach?

author: dev
text: I built it to BD-103, which says email at breach. Was there a change?

author: zara
text: No idea, I'll ask Maya when she's back.

author: priya
text: Sprint 2: dark mode is go. Spec is in BD-105: follow the OS theme by default, with a Light / Dark / System toggle. BD-106 is the theme token refactor that has to land first.

author: kenji
text: I'll do BD-106 first, then BD-105.

author: kenji
text: Do we really need the System option? Light/Dark would be simpler.

author: priya
text: No, keep System and make it the default, exactly as BD-105 says. Most people never touch the setting.

author: priya
text: Decision after the design review: the theme toggle lives in Settings > Appearance, not in the navbar. I've updated BD-105 to say so.

author: kenji
text: Works for me, cleaner navbar anyway.

author: kenji
text: Dark mode PR is up: Light/Dark/System, System default, toggle under Settings > Appearance.

author: priya
text: Checked the dark mode build, matches the ticket. Shipping it 🎉
